title: Session with Edmund Faucher and Father Lewis
summary: Friends visit for informal sessions; Edmund Faucher played with Richards's group after Alcorn left.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: So I changed from one style to another, see? Uh, so right now, as I hear some numbers sometimes, I go out and I try them, I play them. But, uh, I mean, if I had to go out and play a game, all I would like to have would be a guitar and a bass, that's all. That's another. Now sometimes, the fella, a friend of mine, he's a carpenter, his name is Edmund Faucher, he's a musician too. Oh, yeah. You know, you heard him?

Well, he likes, he's a trumpet player, but he's crazy about the bass. And he brings his bass here sometimes, we have a session. I'm trying to get Father Al to come, you know, Father Alfred Lewis? Yeah. Well, that's another guy, see? He, if I could get him and Edmund together, and on the piano, we stayed here all day, because Edmund stayed here from about ten in the morning till six o'clock at the evening. He's run over different numbers, see? And, uh, he was listening at the changes that I was making, I was listening at the changes that I was making, just, you know, just, what you would call reminiscent, for old times sake. Now, Edmund played with us a couple of times, after Alvin left to go away with, uh, to play with Ory. Well, he was a very, very nice trumpet player then. And, uh, he played with me. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
